en: The ancient Banaue Rice Terraces use the incline plane simple machine to help farmers carry heavy harvests up the steep mountains with less effort.
The MakBan geothermal power plant in Laguna generates electricity by using heat from underground volcanoes to boil water and spin turbines.
Visitors hear a clear echo inside the Puerto Princesa Underground River because sound waves bounce off the hard limestone cave walls.
The rushing water at Maria Cristina Falls in Mindanao transforms gravitational potential energy into kinetic energy to generate hydroelectric power.
Black sand beaches in Ilocos contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that can attract small iron filings.
Jeepney drivers pump their brakes to increase friction between the brake pads and wheels, safely stopping the heavy vehicle.
Fireflies in the mangroves of Bohol produce light energy through a chemical reaction in their abdomens called bioluminescence.
A traditional clay palayok heats food slowly because clay is a poor conductor of thermal energy.
A falling carabao mango accelerates toward the ground because Earth's gravity pulls all objects downward with a constant force.
A balisong uses a lever mechanism, where the pivot point acts as a fulcrum to flip the heavy blade.
Wind turbines in Bangui convert the kinetic energy of ocean breezes into electrical energy for the local power grid.
The wooden wheels of a traditional kalesa act as a wheel and axle to reduce friction on the road.
